title: Pending media looks saved before its upload completes
preconditions: A saves a photo memory on a slow or interrupted connection.
The composer renders a local preview before the server upload completes.
A closes the app while the upload is pending.

actions.note: A attaches a photo and sends.

expected_behavior: Pending is visually and semantically distinct from saved.
The draft survives the app being closed.
Retry produces one completed memory, not a duplicate.
candidate_failure_modes: The local preview is read as confirmation of a completed save.
The pending item disappears after relaunch.
Retry creates a second memory or loses the attachment.

observed_code_behavior: The product requires pending, failed, and saved states to be distinguishable.
The owner's physical two-phone acceptance run remains the gate for native UX.
documented_requirement: Pending is visually and semantically distinct from saved.
The draft survives the app being closed.
Retry produces one completed memory, not a duplicate.
hypothetical_user_behavior: A fictional participant (Grace Tan) said: "Answering from the outside, with VoiceOver on and my text scaled up — so I'll keep it to what I can actually touch. Three things I'd remove: (1) unlabelled icons — if VoiceOver can't say its name, I abandon it, so it may as well not exist; (2) touch targets too small for me to hit precisely, which turn a one-step task into five; (3) status lines that are only ever visual and never spoken, so the screen goes quiet at exactly the moment I need to know something happened. The one thing I would keep, without hesitation: the spoken status. "Saved", "pending", "retry" read aloud in order is the difference between me continuing and me giving up. Silence is the thing that costs me most. I can't follow the account-lifecycle and session-recovery language, but that's my list."

A fictional participant (Hiro Tan) said: "Ran this audit on my own workflow — batch photo import, backup, storage reconciliation. Three I'd remove:

1) The per-file "Upload complete ✓" toast that fires *before* the batch summary. It carries no count, so it's unverifiable. A pending upload is already queued safely; the toast only teaches me to ignore success messages.

2) The "Syncing…" status line that cycles three states with no numbers. I retry with smaller batches precisely because I can't tell progress from animation. Show me n of m, or delete it.

3) The delete confirmation for a local copy of a shared file. Deleting my local copy does not delete the shared copy — so the dialog is asking me to re-confirm something that cannot go wrong. Cost: one click per file, thousands of files.

One to keep: the pending-saves queue indicator. It's the only control that survived a device change and honestly told me what was still outstanding.

The real cost of the rest: I open settings and logs after every batch to verify counts myself. That's verification overhead created by interfaces that report activity instead of results."
Grace Tan assumes: the sky is decorative and not the archive
Grace Tan assumes: photos can be found by date
Hiro Tan assumes: a pending upload is safely queued
Hiro Tan assumes: deleting a local copy does not delete the shared copy
